name: Kuiper Belt
tagline: A frozen ring of icy worlds beyond Neptune — the solar system's deep-freeze archive.

facts.label: Composition
facts.value: Water, methane and ammonia ices; tholin-dark surfaces

history: The Kuiper belt is a vast donut of icy bodies orbiting beyond Neptune, the frozen remnant of the solar system's formation preserved like a deep-freeze archive. Gerard Kuiper predicted it in 1951, but the first object beyond Pluto wasn't confirmed until 1992 — since then thousands of Kuiper-belt objects have been catalogued, including dwarf planets Pluto, Eris, Makemake and Haumea. Eris's discovery in 2005 — a body more massive than Pluto — forced the 2006 redefinition that demoted Pluto and created the dwarf-planet class. NASA's New Horizons flew through the belt in 2015 to reveal Pluto's nitrogen glaciers and heart-shaped plain, then visited Arrokoth in 2019 — the most distant object ever explored, a pristine contact binary unchanged for 4.5 billion years. Short-period comets like Halley's originate here, and the belt's outer edge may hide further dwarf planets yet undiscovered.
